Scatterpolar line objects

Source: R/zz-gen-scatterpolar.R
go_scatterpolar_line.Rd

The object for the line of a scatterpolar trace (go_scatterpolar()). go_scatterpolar_line() creates one, with exactly its properties; a named list with the same properties works too.

Usage

go_scatterpolar_line(
  ...,
  backoff = NULL,
  color = NULL,
  dash = NULL,
  shape = NULL,
  smoothing = NULL,
  width = NULL,
  skip_invalid = FALSE
)

Arguments

...

Not for properties, which must be named in full: an abbreviated or unknown name is an error that suggests the right one.

backoff

Sets the line back off from the end point of the nth line segment (in px). This option is useful e.g. to avoid overlap with arrowhead markers. With "auto" the lines would trim before markers if `marker.angleref` is set to "previous". Number in the interval [0, Inf], or a vector of these.

color

Sets the line color. Color: a CSS color string or R color name.

dash

Sets the dash style of lines. Set to a dash type string ("solid", "dot", "dash", "longdash", "dashdot", or "longdashdot") or a dash length list in px (eg "5px,10px,2px,2px"). One of "solid", "dot", "dash", "longdash", "dashdot", "longdashdot", or a string matching "^\\d+(\\.\\d+)?(px|%)?((,|\\s)\\s*\\d+(\\.\\d+)?(px|%)?)*$".

shape

Determines the line shape. With "spline" the lines are drawn using spline interpolation. The other available values correspond to step-wise line shapes. One of "linear", "spline".

smoothing

Has an effect only if `shape` is set to "spline" Sets the amount of smoothing. 0 corresponds to no smoothing (equivalent to a "linear" shape). Number in the interval [0, 1.3].

width

Sets the line width (in px). Number in the interval [0, Inf].

skip_invalid

If TRUE, silently drop invalid properties instead of raising an error.

Value

A go_scatterpolar_line object (a named list).

Details

Nested objects are named lists, or objects of the constructors their arguments name. Every property is checked against the plotly.js schema when the object is created or modified. A property may be a one-sided formula (color = ~col): it is kept, and evaluated in the data (then checked) when its trace is added to a figure with add_<trace>() or add_trace().

Examples

mtcars |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_scatterpolar(
    r = ~mpg,
    theta = ~hp,
    line = go_scatterpolar_line(color = "red")
  )
